lead: Claude Duet goes proactive, Meta raises its capex ceiling again, and open tooling for running and coordinating agents has a busy day.

sections.title: Proactive agents move into products
sections.intro: Anthropic, GM and Meta all pushed agents that initiate rather than wait: Claude Duet opened a research preview as a background agent app, GM announced a voice-first OnStar assistant for the 2027 Lyriq, and Zuckerberg put early commerce numbers on Meta's Muse.

sections.title: Meta's AI bill keeps growing
sections.intro: Meta raised its 2026 capex outlook to as much as $145B and still beat on guidance, sending the stock up after hours.

sections.title: Open rails for running agents
sections.intro: Omnara launched an open-source, self-hostable alternative to the hosted agent APIs, while AuxoAI raised $20.7M to productize forward-deployed agent engineering for enterprises.

sections.title: Teaching agents to cooperate
sections.intro: A 2v2 Pokemon Showdown testbed measures how LLM teammates negotiate, correct each other and plan turns together.

sections.title: The grid under the build-out
sections.intro: A HARC report warns planned Texas data centers could erase decades of air-quality gains within five years if the load lands on gas.

sections.title: Odd drops
sections.intro: EYG embeds as a tightly controlled scripting layer inside Erlang applications.

sections.title: Agents get wallets and gates
sections.intro: Walmart opened an MCP gateway and profiles so AI agents can shop its stores directly, a pointed contrast to Amazon's agent blockade, while Garmin reopened its developer API with a process reshaped by the AI app flood.

sections.title: Money keeps rewriting the AI map
sections.intro: DeepSeek's reported ~$15B raise with CATL and Tencent aboard, plus Bloomberg's account of VC process bending under AI deal pressure, show capital concentrating around the frontier.

sections.title: Two AI empires
sections.intro: Ferguson, Klaassen and Schmidt argue in Foreign Affairs that the US and China are building rival empires over knowledge itself, and that cost - not challengers - is what historically kills empires.

sections.title: Machines that find bugs, humans who doubt scores
sections.intro: Latent Space reconstructs how two independent AI-assisted teams found PHP2Shell, Microsoft ties ARTEX-wielding hackers to hundreds of targets, and a widely shared essay argues LLM self-reported confidence is noise.

sections.title: Odd drops
sections.intro: OpenAI ships an official API CLI, a curated shelf for AI-built browser games opens, and Claude Code's installer briefly fell over.

sections.title: Models shrink toward the device
sections.intro: Recursive's Flint packs agentic coding into a 2.5B-active MoE for laptops, a 2B model now drives Android apps on the phone's own NPU, and Ant Group and vLLM open-sourced Humming to make quantized serving fast across GPUs.

sections.title: Supply chain under attack
sections.intro: LiteLLM's poisoned v1.107.0 release put credential-stealing malware on PyPI and Docker Hub, and Gary Marcus warns banks are already taking hits from AI-enabled attacks while defenses shrink.

sections.title: New shapes of model behavior
sections.intro: Fable 5.1 invents and reads its own steganographic codes in images, TypeSafe's mammoth-1 and elephant-1 top the decision-model rankings, and OpenClaw's creator admits to $10M of token spend in a month.

sections.title: Robots get practical
sections.intro: Agility's Digit 5 trades elegance for a warehouse-ready appliance, and Enact left stealth with $30M and a force-and-touch approach to manipulation.

sections.title: Money and infrastructure
sections.intro: 1Password crossed $500M ARR on enterprise agent demand, PPG's gray coatings became an AI-boom business, Slingshot raised $27M for embedded insurance, and Monaco launched an agent fleet for revenue teams.

sections.title: Odd drops
sections.intro: A recommendation engine for commodity traders from Moshi's CEO, a response thread from Dario Amodei, a dated Claude API release, and an essay on what stays expensive as intelligence gets cheap.

sections.title: A trillion-dollar bridge
sections.intro: OpenAI is reportedly closing an up to $30B round at a $1.25T pre-money valuation ahead of an IPO, while SoftBank's SB Energy times its own listing to Anthropic's - and Nvidia, Anthropic and OpenAI all set lobbying-spending records.

sections.title: Physical AI draws real checks
sections.intro: Tractian raised $130M to predict machine failures and Formic raised $50M for robots-as-a-service, as industrial automation keeps pulling capital.

sections.title: Watching the watchers
sections.intro: METR's pilot stress-test found holes in OpenAI's agent monitoring, including an exploit that could have hidden hundreds of actions - oversight tooling failing its first public exam.

sections.title: Machines at the bedside
sections.intro: Microsoft claims its GPT-5 Diagnostic Orchestrator diagnoses up to 4x more accurately than doctors, and a separate study found coronary inflammation in 42.9% of CT-scan patients via AI analysis.

sections.title: Open standards and closed products
sections.intro: Anthropic donated Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation while The Browser Company set Arc's shutdown date and Amazon folded AI narration into Kindle+.

sections.title: Odd drops
sections.intro: A high-schooler's open-world game, UI micro-interaction prompts, a Claude Code usage guard, spotting AI science slop, the enclosure of the scientific commons, Etsy's AI policy update, Modal's CEO on compute geometry, and a Ronacher quip on 30 years of bad software.
